symbols.name: d
symbols.def: The prespecified number of outcome coordinates.

symbols.name: G
symbols.def: The number of randomized clusters.

symbols.name: N_i
symbols.role: Number of labeled individuals in cluster \(i\).

symbols.name: \mathcal R_i
symbols.def: The labels and all preassignment variables for the \(N_i\) target individuals in cluster \(i\).

symbols.name: \mathcal B
symbols.def: The support of complete cluster-level preassignment records, including variable-length rosters.

symbols.name: B_i
symbols.def: The observed preassignment record containing \(N_i\), \(\mathcal R_i\), and every roster variable used by assignment or response models.

symbols.name: \mathcal C
symbols.def: The prespecified finite support of response-model strata.

symbols.name: C_i
symbols.def: \(C_i=g_{\mathrm{resp}}(B_i)\).

symbols.name: \mathcal S_k
symbols.def: The prespecified finite support of outcome coordinate \(k\), oriented so that larger values are better.

symbols.name: \mathcal S
symbols.def: Each finite coordinate set is oriented so that larger values are better.

symbols.name: \operatorname{pr}_m
symbols.def: The projection retaining exactly the coordinates marked observed by \(m\), with \(\mathcal S_m=\prod_{k:m_k=1}\mathcal S_k\).

symbols.name: O_{ij}
symbols.def: \(O_{ij}=(B_i,A_i,M_{ij}(A_i),\operatorname{pr}_{M_{ij}(A_i)}Y_{ij}(A_i))\).

symbols.name: \nu
symbols.def: \(\nu=\mathbb E[N_i]\).

symbols.name: \mathbb P^{\star}
symbols.def: The law obtained by sampling a cluster with probability proportional to \(N_i\) and then sampling one of its \(N_i\) roster members uniformly.

symbols.name: \kappa
symbols.def: \(\kappa(c)=\mathbb P^{\star}(C_i=c)\).

symbols.name: \mathcal C_{+}
symbols.def: \(\mathcal C_{+}=\{c\in\mathcal C:\kappa(c)>0\}\). Strata outside \(\mathcal C_{+}\) have zero individual-weighted mass and are omitted from every conditional-law and linear-program index set.

symbols.name: H_a
symbols.role: Observed-law right-hand side for arm \(a\) on positive-mass strata.

symbols.name: \Gamma
symbols.def: The maximal multiplicative departure of a response-pattern probability from its response-stratum marginal frequency.

symbols.name: q_a
symbols.role: Individual-weighted joint mass of response stratum and complete potential state.

symbols.name: R
symbols.def: \(R=\{(s_0,s_1):s_{1k}\ge s_{0k}\text{ for every }k,\ s_1\ne s_0\}\).

symbols.name: \beta
symbols.def: \(\beta=\mathbb P^{\star}((Y_{ij}(0),Y_{ij}(1))\in R)\).

symbols.name: x
symbols.def: The vector concatenating \(\lambda_0,\lambda_1,q_0,q_1,\pi\) in a fixed lexicographic order.

symbols.name: \bar h
symbols.def: The vector stacking \(H_0,H_1\) and zeros for all completion and coupling consistency equations.

symbols.name: E
symbols.role: Matrix encoding observed projections, arm-state completion, and coupling marginals on \(\mathcal C_{+}\).

symbols.name: G_{\Gamma}
symbols.role: Matrix encoding the two-sided response-pattern sensitivity restrictions on \(\mathcal C_{+}\).

symbols.name: c_R
symbols.def: The entries corresponding to \(\pi(c,s_0,s_1)\) equal \(\mathbf 1\{(s_0,s_1)\in R\}\), and all other entries equal zero.

symbols.name: \mathcal F_{\Gamma}(H)
symbols.role: All arm completions and cross-world couplings on \(\mathcal C_{+}\) compatible with the response-pattern law and sensitivity index.

symbols.name: \Gamma_{\mathrm{feas}}
symbols.role: Smallest sensitivity index at which the observed response-pattern law admits a full-data completion and cross-world coupling.

symbols.name: L_{\Gamma}
symbols.role: Minimum Pareto-benefit mass over the joint feasible polytope.

symbols.name: U_{\Gamma}
symbols.role: Maximum Pareto-benefit mass over the joint feasible polytope.

symbols.name: \ell_a
symbols.role: Coordinatewise minimum of \(q_a(c,s)\) over arm-specific feasible completions.

symbols.name: u_a
symbols.role: Coordinatewise maximum of \(q_a(c,s)\) over arm-specific feasible completions.

symbols.name: \mathcal F^{\mathrm{rect}}_{\Gamma}(H)
symbols.role: The relaxation retaining only statewise envelopes, normalization, and generic cross-world transport.

symbols.name: \mathsf W
symbols.role: A three-binary-outcome law with pairwise observation patterns showing strict nonrectangularity.

symbols.name: \Gamma_{\mathrm{maj}}
symbols.role: Smallest sensitivity index admitting a compatible law with at most one-half Pareto benefit.

symbols.name: \mathfrak H_R
symbols.role: Hypergraph-incidence starting point for an interpretable combinatorial dual.

assumptions.condition: The cluster records \(\{(B_i,\{Y_{ij}(a),M_{ij}(a):j\le N_i,a\in\{0,1\}\}) : i=1,\ldots,G\}\) are independent and identically distributed.
The complete labeled roster \(\mathcal R_i\), its size \(N_i\), and every roster variable entering assignment or response models are observed before \(A_i\) and are included in \(B_i\).

novel.justification: A closed enrollment registry with prespecified baseline forms records every eligible label and every design or follow-up predictor before cluster assignment. This contract is empirically auditable and separates outcome nonresponse from unobserved recruitment.

assumptions.condition: Each \(Y_{ij}(a)\) and \(M_{ij}(a)\) depends only on its own cluster assignment \(a\).

standard.name: Cluster-level stable unit treatment value assumption

assumptions.condition: The realized response pattern and observed outcome components equal \(M_{ij}(A_i)\) and \(\operatorname{pr}_{M_{ij}(A_i)}Y_{ij}(A_i)\), respectively.

For every \(a\in\{0,1\}\), \(c\in\mathcal C_{+}\), \(m\in\mathcal M\), and \(s\in\mathcal S\) with \(\mathbb P^{\star}(Y_{ij}(a)=s\mid C_i=c)>0\), \(\Gamma^{-1}r_a(m\mid c)\le\mathbb P^{\star}(M_{ij}(a)=m\mid C_i=c,Y_{ij}(a)=s)\le\Gamma r_a(m\mid c)\).

novel.justification: Follow-up audits can bound how much any complete clinical state is overrepresented or underrepresented in each vector response pattern among patients in the same prespecified response stratum. Because \(C_i=g_{\mathrm{resp}}(B_i)\), every stratifying variable and the full roster are recorded before assignment. The index has a direct likelihood-ratio interpretation, and \(\Gamma=1\) is vector restricted missing at random without requiring complete-case positivity.

definitions.name: Identified response-pattern laws
definitions.construction: For \(c\in\mathcal C_{+}\), \(m\in\mathcal M\), and \(z_m\in\mathcal S_m\), set \(H_a(c,m,z_m)=\nu^{-1}\mathbb E[e_a(B_i)^{-1}\mathbf 1\{A_i=a,C_i=c\}\sum_{j=1}^{N_i}\mathbf 1\{M_{ij}(A_i)=m,\operatorname{pr}_mY_{ij}(A_i)=z_m\}]\) and \(r_a(m\mid c)=\kappa(c)^{-1}\sum_{z_m}H_a(c,m,z_m)\). No conditional response law is defined for \(c\notin\mathcal C_{+}\); such strata have zero \(\mathbb P^{\star}\)-mass and are omitted from the linear program.

definitions.name: Joint missing-state and cross-world feasible polytope
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal F_{\Gamma}(H)\) is the set of nonnegative \(x=(\lambda_0,\lambda_1,q_0,q_1,\pi)\) satisfying, for every \(a\in\{0,1\}\), \(c\in\mathcal C_{+}\), \(m\in\mathcal M\), \(s,z_m,s_0,s_1\) in their declared finite state spaces, \(\sum_{s:\operatorname{pr}_m(s)=z_m}\lambda_a(c,s,m)=H_a(c,m,z_m)\), \(q_a(c,s)=\sum_m\lambda_a(c,s,m)\), \(\Gamma^{-1}r_a(m\mid c)q_a(c,s)\le\lambda_a(c,s,m)\le\Gamma r_a(m\mid c)q_a(c,s)\), \(\sum_{s_1}\pi(c,s_0,s_1)=q_0(c,s_0)\), and \(\sum_{s_0}\pi(c,s_0,s_1)=q_1(c,s_1)\). Equivalently, \(\mathcal F_{\Gamma}(H)=\{x\ge0:Ex=\bar h,\ G_{\Gamma}x\le0\}\), where \(E\) and \(G_{\Gamma}\) are the finite coefficient matrices of the displayed constraints indexed by \(\mathcal C_{+}\), \(\mathcal M\), and \(\mathcal S\). Strata in \(\mathcal C\setminus\mathcal C_{+}\) contribute zero individual-weighted mass and generate no completion, coupling, or sensitivity rows.

definitions.name: Joint sharp endpoints
definitions.construction: For every finite \(\Gamma\ge\Gamma_{\mathrm{feas}}\), define \(L_{\Gamma}=\min_{x\in\mathcal F_{\Gamma}(H)}c_R^{\mathsf T}x\), \(U_{\Gamma}=\max_{x\in\mathcal F_{\Gamma}(H)}c_R^{\mathsf T}x\), and \(\mathcal I_{\Gamma}(H)=[L_{\Gamma},U_{\Gamma}]\).

definitions.name: Statewise-envelope rectangular relaxation
definitions.construction: For each arm and \(c\in\mathcal C_{+}\), let \(\ell_a(c,s)=\min q_a(c,s)\) and \(u_a(c,s)=\max q_a(c,s)\) over the arm-specific \((\lambda_a,q_a)\) block satisfying the projection, completion, and sensitivity constraints in \(\mathcal F_{\Gamma}(H)\). Define \(\mathcal F^{\mathrm{rect}}_{\Gamma}(H)\) as the set of nonnegative \((q_0,q_1,\pi)\) satisfying \(\ell_a(c,s)\le q_a(c,s)\le u_a(c,s)\), \(\sum_s q_a(c,s)=\kappa(c)\), \(\sum_{s_1}\pi(c,s_0,s_1)=q_0(c,s_0)\), and \(\sum_{s_0}\pi(c,s_0,s_1)=q_1(c,s_1)\) for every state index and every \(c\in\mathcal C_{+}\). This relaxation retains the statewise envelopes but discards the joint cross-state projection equalities.

definitions.name: Three-coordinate pair-pattern witness
definitions.construction: In one response stratum, let \(\mathcal S=\{0,1\}^3\) in lexicographic order and let the three response patterns \(110,101,011\) each have probability \(1/3\), independently of the full state. Conditional on these patterns, respectively, the control projection masses on \(00,01,10,11\) are \((1,1,2,2)/6\), \((1,1,3,1)/6\), and \((2,1,2,1)/6\); the treatment projection masses are \((0,0,2,4)/6\), \((0,0,3,3)/6\), and \((1,1,2,2)/6\). The complete arm-state masses \(q_0=(1,0,0,1,1,1,2,0)/6\) and \(q_1=(0,0,0,0,1,1,2,2)/6\) generate these projections. Denote this observed law by \(\mathsf W\).

definitions.name: Sensitivity threshold for guaranteed majority benefit
Hypergraph certificate handle
definitions.construction: Handle: form \(\mathfrak H_R\) from one vertex class for complete states, one for observed projections \(\operatorname{pr}_m(s)\), and one for strict-dominance edges; label its signed incidence rows by the equality and sensitivity rows of \(E\) and \(G_{\Gamma}\), then study balancedness and network-matrix representations of this incidence system.

statements.statement: The finite-index feasible domain is empty exactly when \(\Gamma_{\mathrm{feas}}=\infty\). If \(\Gamma_{\mathrm{feas}}<\infty\), then the onset is attained and \(\mathcal F_{\Gamma}(H)\ne\varnothing\) holds exactly for finite \(\Gamma\ge\Gamma_{\mathrm{feas}}\). Thus \(\Gamma<\Gamma_{\mathrm{feas}}\) means that the indexed response-selection restriction is incompatible with the observed response-pattern law, rather than that the data fail to guarantee majority benefit.
statements.justification: The onset separates model-data incompatibility from an adverse causal conclusion along the sensitivity path.
statements.gap: Scharfstein, Manski, and Anthony, Section 5.2, note that empirically constrained missing-ordinal programs can be infeasible and propose penalized slacks; the present population-law statement instead characterizes the exact no-slack compatibility domain of the joint response-pattern and cross-world program.
statements.consumer: A trial report can flag sensitivity values below the onset as refuted by the response-pattern law before interpreting any Pareto-benefit bound.

statements.statement: For every finite \(\Gamma\ge\Gamma_{\mathrm{feas}}\), under the stated information contract, the sharp identified set for \(\beta\) over all compatible cluster potential-outcome and vector-response laws satisfying the \(\Gamma\)-selection restriction is exactly \(\mathcal I_{\Gamma}(H)=[L_{\Gamma},U_{\Gamma}]\). All conditional response laws and all rows of \(\mathcal F_{\Gamma}(H)\) are indexed only by \(c\in\mathcal C_{+}\); strata with \(\kappa(c)=0\) contribute zero individual-weighted mass and require no conditional-law version. Both endpoints and every intermediate value are attained. Every compatible law maps into \(\mathcal F_{\Gamma}(H)\), and every point of \(\mathcal F_{\Gamma}(H)\) can be embedded in a cluster law that reproduces \(H_0,H_1\) on \(\mathcal C_{+}\), the observed complete roster distribution, and the known randomization. Moreover, finite-dimensional strong duality gives attained certificates \(L_{\Gamma}=\max_{\alpha\text{ unrestricted},\ \eta\ge0}\{\bar h^{\mathsf T}\alpha:E^{\mathsf T}\alpha-G_{\Gamma}^{\mathsf T}\eta\le c_R\}\) and \(U_{\Gamma}=\min_{\alpha\text{ unrestricted},\ \eta\ge0}\{\bar h^{\mathsf T}\alpha:E^{\mathsf T}\alpha+G_{\Gamma}^{\mathsf T}\eta\ge c_R\}\).
statements.justification: The theorem prevents loss of sharpness at the interface between multivariate missing-state completion and same-person causal coupling.
statements.gap: Scharfstein, Manski, and Anthony constrain scalar two-occasion follow-up laws and compare arm distributions. Gao, Ge, and Qian, Ji, Lei, and Spector, and Ober-Reynolds optimize over fixed or already available arm marginals. Fan, Park, Pass, and Shi characterize conditional optimal transport when the two source laws of \((Y_1,X)\) and \((Y_0,X)\) are identified. That two-source model and the present overlapping response-pattern model are non-nested, and none of these results characterizes the present latent arm-state completion polytope jointly with the cross-world Pareto coupling.
statements.consumer: A PPACT companion analysis can report a certified range for the fraction of enrolled patients whose complete treated outcome vector strictly Pareto-dominates their complete control vector despite incomplete component records.

statements.statement: For the law \(\mathsf W\) at \(\Gamma=1\), the exact joint program gives \(\mathcal I_1(\mathsf W)=[1/6,8/9]\). The statewise-envelope rectangular relaxation gives upper endpoint \(1\): it admits the control vector \((1,1,1,0,2,0,1,0)/6\) and treatment vector \((0,0,0,0,1,1,2,2)/6\), which possess an all-benefit coupling, although the displayed control vector violates the overlapping pair-projection equations. This finite construction is an internal nonrectangularity diagnostic: replacing the exact completion polytope by its statewise rectangular envelope before transport loses response-pattern restrictions and strictly enlarges the feasible range.
statements.justification: A strict finite gap establishes that the joint completion-and-coupling geometry is substantive rather than an artifact of notation.
statements.gap: The diagnostic makes no claim about a published imputation workflow. It isolates the information discarded by the internally defined statewise-envelope relaxation and thereby explains the theorem's nonrectangular feasible set.
statements.consumer: Analysts can use the finite table as a reproducible unit test for implementations of the exact joint program and its deliberately coarser rectangular benchmark.

statements.statement: Suppose \(\Gamma_{\mathrm{feas}}<\infty\). On the feasible domain \(\Gamma\in[\Gamma_{\mathrm{feas}},\infty)\), the sets \(\mathcal F_{\Gamma}(H)\) are nested and \(L_{\Gamma}\) is nonincreasing. If \(\Gamma_{\mathrm{maj}}<\infty\), the infimum in its definition is attained. Guaranteed strict majority benefit holds exactly for feasible \(\Gamma<\Gamma_{\mathrm{maj}}\), equivalently \(L_{\Gamma}>1/2\); at and above a finite \(\Gamma_{\mathrm{maj}}\), an observationally compatible law has \(\beta\le1/2\). If \(\Gamma_{\mathrm{maj}}=\infty\), every finite feasible sensitivity value guarantees \(\beta>1/2\). Values \(\Gamma<\Gamma_{\mathrm{feas}}\) are model-data incompatibilities and carry no majority-benefit interpretation. Both thresholds are computable to any prescribed rational tolerance by monotone linear-feasibility searches.
statements.justification: The threshold converts an indexed missingness departure into the exact point where a clinically interpretable majority claim ceases to be forced by the data.
statements.gap: Huang, Fang, Hanley, and Rosenblum study confidence intervals for a scalar ordinal or binary fraction benefiting in randomized trials, while existing cluster-trial sensitivity analyses target smooth average effects. Neither result propagates vector response-pattern selection through the same-person strict-Pareto event.
statements.consumer: A data-monitoring committee can state how large pattern-specific outcome selection must be before the conclusion that most patients benefit is no longer guaranteed.

statements.statement: If \(M_{ij}(a)=(1,\ldots,1)\) almost surely in both arms, then \(\Gamma_{\mathrm{feas}}=1\), \(q_a=H_a\) is point identified, the sensitivity inequalities are redundant for every finite \(\Gamma\ge1\), and \(\mathcal I_{\Gamma}(H)\) reduces to the ordinary sharp optimal-transport interval for the strict Pareto cost with fixed arm marginals.
statements.justification: The reduction is the required sanity check and fixes the relationship to established marginal optimal-transport bounds.
statements.gap: The known complete-response result is recovered as a boundary case; the contribution is the nonrectangular observed-data completion that disappears in this case.
statements.consumer: Implementers obtain an exact regression test against standard finite optimal-transport software when all outcome components are observed.

statements.statement: For which response-pattern families and finite product orders does the signed incidence system \(\mathfrak H_R\) admit a network-matrix or balanced-hypergraph representation that reduces both joint endpoints to a single polynomial-size min-cut or submodular-flow problem, returns an extremal completion and cross-world coupling, and yields an integral explanatory certificate when \(H_a\) is rational? Establish a necessary-and-sufficient structural characterization or prove a non-representability frontier.
statements.justification: The generic linear program certifies sharpness, but a structural frontier would identify exactly when clinicians can receive cut-like explanations rather than opaque dual vectors.
statements.gap: Strassen-type transport networks cover fixed marginals, whereas overlapping missing-data projections create hyperedges whose network representability is not characterized by the cited causal or missing-data results.
statements.consumer: Software for prespecified multivariate trial endpoints could automatically select a transparent min-cut certificate when the response design permits one and otherwise report why a generic linear-program certificate is unavoidable.

sampling_model.design: Independent cluster Bernoulli assignment with known \(e(B_i)\).
sampling_model.units: A complete labeled preassignment roster is observed for every cluster, with \(0<\mathbb E[N_i]<\infty\); identification targets the individual-weighted superpopulation law \(\mathbb P^{\star}\).
sampling_model.treatment: Treatment \(A_i\) is assigned at cluster level under cluster SUTVA.
sampling_model.missingness: The vector response pattern is observed. For each \(c\in\mathcal C_{+}\), its selection probability given complete state is bounded relative to the pattern frequency within the finite prespecified stratum \(C_i=g_{\mathrm{resp}}(B_i)\); \(\kappa\)-null strata define no conditional response law and are omitted from the program.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: None is asserted. The identification theorem takes the finite response-pattern laws \(H_0,H_1\) as observed-law inputs.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: We propose a doubly robust estimator for the average treatment effect on a variety of effect measure scales.
We present two complementary approaches for constructing bounds under assumptions on the missing data mechanism considered plausible by scientific experts.
Many causal estimands are only partially identifiable since they depend on the unobservable joint distribution between potential outcomes.
The sharp identified set is an interval with endpoints characterized by the value of optimal transport problems.
We cast the causal partial identification problem in the framework of MOT with \(K\) margins and \(d\)-dimensional outcomes and obtain the exact partial identified set.
We establish a novel characterization of the identified set for the true parameter in terms of a continuum of inequalities defined by conditional optimal transport.
The self-censoring model is identified under a completeness condition.
The existence of probability measures with given marginals is characterized under support restrictions.
Sharp bounds are established for causal estimands comparing two ordinal potential outcomes.
Constructing a confidence interval for the fraction who benefit from treatment, using randomized trial data.

tldr: A complete trial roster and finite positive mean roster size identify individual-weighted vector response-pattern laws on \(\mathcal C_{+}=\{c:\kappa(c)>0\}\); null strata contribute no mass and enter neither conditional laws nor linear-program rows. The overlapping projection equations define nonrectangular feasible arm-state distributions, which must be optimized jointly with the same-person cross-world Pareto coupling. The central theorem gives the attained sharp interval and joint dual certificates for every sensitivity index in the compatible domain beginning at \(\Gamma_{\mathrm{feas}}\). A distinct breakdown point \(\Gamma_{\mathrm{maj}}\) marks when a compatible law first permits at most one-half of patients to benefit. A three-binary-outcome internal diagnostic has joint upper endpoint \(8/9\) but rectangular-relaxation endpoint \(1\).

project_justification.gap: Cluster-trial missing-data methods target smooth average effects; Scharfstein, Manski, and Anthony bound scalar ordinal follow-up distributions; and randomized-trial fraction-benefiting methods treat scalar ordinal or binary outcomes. Gao, Ge, and Qian use fixed identified arm marginals. Fan, Park, Pass, and Shi use two identified source laws \((Y_1,X)\) and \((Y_0,X)\). Neither optimal-transport information structure preserves the nonrectangular restrictions from overlapping vector response patterns while simultaneously completing latent arm-state laws and ranging over the same-person potential-outcome coupling.
project_justification.niche: Finite multivariate outcomes with nonmonotone component response patterns create a tractable but genuinely joint observed-data and cross-world partial-identification problem.
project_justification.fill: The project gives the exact feasible polytope on positive-mass response strata, its compatibility onset, an attained sharp interval with primal observational embeddings and joint dual certificates, an internal finite diagnostic proving strict loss from statewise rectangularization, and a separate response-selection breakdown threshold for guaranteed majority benefit.

related_work: Wang, Li, and Wang provide the restricted-missing-at-random benchmark for incomplete outcomes and informative cluster sizes, but their estimand is a smooth average effect; their work informs the roster and missingness contract. Scharfstein, Manski, and Anthony study an ordinal outcome measured twice with the second measurement missing: Sections 2--4, especially equations (9)--(10) and (12)--(20), bound the scalar follow-up law under monotonicity and indexed selection restrictions; Section 5.2 discusses infeasible empirical constraint systems; and Section 6, equations (23)--(24), compares interventions through an arm-distribution stochastic-dominance measure. That program neither has overlapping vector response patterns nor couples two potential outcome vectors for a same-person strict-Pareto event. Huang, Fang, Hanley, and Rosenblum construct confidence intervals for a scalar ordinal or binary fraction benefiting in randomized trials; their target differs from vector strict-Pareto benefit under response-pattern selection and a jointly optimized missing-state and cross-world set. Gao, Ge, and Qian define the causal set in Section 1.2, equation (2), by ranging over couplings whose \(K\) arm marginals are fixed, and Section 2.2, equation (3), retains those fixed-marginal constraints for multi-marginal optimal transport. Their exact fixed-marginal MOT cannot encode arm marginals that are themselves endogenous completion variables tied across states by overlapping response-pattern projection equations. Fan, Park, Pass, and Shi study a different incomplete-data structure: Section 1.1, equation (1), defines a moment model in \((Y_1,Y_0,X)\); Section 2, Assumption 2.1(ii)--(iii), takes the laws of \((Y_1,X)\) and \((Y_0,X)\) as identified from two data sources; and Theorem 3.1 characterizes the resulting set by conditional optimal transport. The models are non-nested: their source laws are identified but no within-vector response-pattern completion is present, whereas the present response-pattern projections only partially identify each latent complete arm state before the cross-world coupling is chosen. Thus the present proposal does not claim that generic incomplete-data conditional optimal transport is absent. Ji, Lei, and Spector and Ober-Reynolds likewise inform the coupling component after arm laws or conditional arm laws are available. Strassen supplies the classical marginal-coupling principle behind the complete-response check. Li, Miao, Shpitser, and Tchetgen Tchetgen identify multivariate nonmonotone missing-data laws under self-censoring and completeness, a different point-identification model. The rectangular-relaxation construction is solely an internal diagnostic and is not attributed to a published imputation procedure. No theorem-level improvement over these comparator results is claimed.
technical_internal_limitation: The finite rectangular-relaxation witness is an internal diagnostic of the proposed geometry, not a claim that a named published estimator or imputation procedure implements that relaxation. Sharpness is relative to the identified individual-weighted response-pattern laws \(H_0,H_1\) on \(\mathcal C_{+}\), the complete roster distribution, and the stated sensitivity restriction. A \(\kappa\)-null stratum has zero individual-weighted contribution and is deliberately absent from every conditional-law and linear-program index set. Structural zeros within positive-mass strata can make \(\Gamma_{\mathrm{feas}}=\infty\), in which case no finite member of the indexed sensitivity model is compatible with the observed law. Higher-order within-cluster observed-outcome dependence is not retained in this information contract and could further contract the identified set. The proposal makes no root-\(G\) inference, bootstrap, efficiency, or PPACT precision claim.
honest_scope: The compatibility-onset proposition, central sharpness theorem, finite nonrectangularity diagnostic, and majority threshold are all to be proved. Every conditional response law and feasible-set row is restricted to \(\mathcal C_{+}\); null strata contribute zero target mass. Majority benefit is interpreted only for finite \(\Gamma\ge\Gamma_{\mathrm{feas}}\); smaller values represent infeasible response models. The complete-response reduction is only a known sanity check and must give \(\Gamma_{\mathrm{feas}}=1\) and ordinary fixed-marginal optimal transport. The exact structural frontier for cut-like certificates in the joint projection-and-dominance system remains the first-class open question. Empirical usefulness at \(106\) clusters and access to a fixed PPACT cohort remain outside this identification core.

seed_details.reason: Multivariate response patterns constrain a common complete-state law through overlapping projections. Combining those nonrectangular constraints with a same-person cross-world coupling is mathematically different from conditioning on richer observed information or applying transport to already identified arm marginals.
The marginal-only capacity angle is excluded by the pivot directive.

literature_map: Thread one concerns missing outcomes. Wang, Li, and Wang handle incomplete cluster-trial outcomes for smooth average effects. Scharfstein, Manski, and Anthony use scalar two-occasion ordinal tables, monotonicity beliefs, and indexed selection models to bound follow-up distributions and an arm-distribution dominance measure. Neither paper forms a multivariate completion polytope from overlapping response patterns and then couples the latent arm states across worlds. Thread two concerns the fraction benefiting: Huang, Fang, Hanley, and Rosenblum give confidence intervals for a scalar ordinal or binary target, not vector strict-Pareto benefit under response-pattern selection. Thread three concerns causal and incomplete-data optimal transport. Gao, Ge, and Qian formulate exact multi-marginal causal bounds over couplings with fixed identified marginals; Ober-Reynolds and Ji, Lei, and Spector likewise start from identified arm laws or conditional arm laws. Fan, Park, Pass, and Shi allow incomplete two-source data but assume the source laws of \((Y_1,X)\) and \((Y_0,X)\) are identified, then characterize moment-model identified sets by conditional optimal transport. That model is non-nested with overlapping vector response patterns, which leave each complete arm-state law latent and constrained by several intersecting projection equations. Thread four concerns multivariate nonmonotone missingness. Li, Miao, Shpitser, and Tchetgen Tchetgen obtain point identification under self-censoring and completeness, whereas the bounded pattern-selection model here yields a finite sensitivity-indexed polytope. Thread five is classical coupling duality: Strassen explains the complete-response reduction, but not transport with projection-linked endogenous marginals. The exact compatibility onset and joint observed-data sharp set remain open across these adjacent threads.

novelty_justification: The closest missing-outcome comparators are Wang, Li, and Wang for smooth average effects in cluster trials and Scharfstein, Manski, and Anthony for bounds on scalar ordinal follow-up laws and arm-distribution dominance. The closest direct fraction-benefiting comparator is Huang, Fang, Hanley, and Rosenblum, whose randomized-trial target is scalar ordinal or binary. Gao, Ge, and Qian provide the clearest fixed-marginal multi-marginal optimal-transport comparator: their Section 1.2, equation (2), and Section 2.2, equation (3), range over couplings with identified marginals, as do the relevant components in Ji, Lei, and Spector and Ober-Reynolds. Fan, Park, Pass, and Shi provide the closest incomplete-data conditional-optimal-transport comparator: Section 2, Assumption 2.1(ii)--(iii), takes \((Y_1,X)\) and \((Y_0,X)\) source laws as identified, and Theorem 3.1 characterizes the corresponding moment-model set. Their model is non-nested with the present one because overlapping component-response patterns do not identify either complete vector arm law; instead they impose intersecting projection restrictions that must be retained while the arm laws and cross-world coupling are jointly chosen. The novelty claim is solely the sharp nonrectangular observed-data set produced by joint missing-state completion and cross-world Pareto transport, together with its observational embeddings and joint dual certificates. The sensitivity-feasibility onset is the domain boundary of that same set, and the finite rectangular construction is an internal strictness diagnostic. Li, Miao, Shpitser, and Tchetgen Tchetgen instead point identify a full-data law under self-censoring and completeness. No strict improvement over any comparator theorem, no absence of generic incomplete-data conditional optimal transport, and no published rectangular-imputation workflow are claimed.
